before.interpretation: Only synthetic dummy credentials were used. A raw voice transport Error was persisted in request history and returned by getPreparedNews. A separate preview transport object with code invalid bypassed the generic IPC error boundary.

changes: Normalize unknown preparation errors before request-history persistence and rethrow. Preserve known ServiceError guidance, no-news/partial coverage and controller-abort uncertainty.
Normalize workflow settlement failures independently and remove raw error objects from tick logs.
Pass specific IPC errors only for ServiceError instances. Convert the three media validation errors to that application type.
Reject explicitly non-audio/non-octet-stream successful speech responses before storing them as audio; absent headers retain prior compatibility.

Migrate ambiguous legacy request/profile failure text to fixed guidance using a persisted preparationErrorVersion marker. Preserve known no-news/partial-coverage reasons, IDs, states, counters, pause settings and artifacts.

Coalesce cold local-state hydration, persist migration outside its broad read fallback and retry failures. Prepared-library migration distinguishes initial missing-index ENOENT from migration-write ENOENT and retries without replacing history with an empty library.

sourceAudit.logs: The only product console logging in src/main is now a fixed workflow-tick message without an error object; renderer/preload have no credential logging.
sourceAudit.connection: JellyfinService.connection returns an explicit non-secret field list. Tokens remain internal; requests authorize through headers and password appears only in the sign-in body.
sourceAudit.providerStatus: Provider key setters/getters return configured/sessionOnly status. Read-key helpers are not bridge methods.
sourceAudit.modelContext: Inspected bounded news/voice request construction includes no connection/provider credentials; native captured request bodies contain no credential markers except the intended Jellyfin sign-in password.
sourceAudit.media: Direct/converted audio uses opaque handles. Artwork URLs use item/tag values and a main-process authorized proxy, not token-bearing URLs. Header routing remains restricted to configured/provider destinations.
sourceAudit.externalOpen: The actual openSource IPC validates HTTP/HTTPS and rejects userinfo. Its final shell sink is captured in the fixture; only two ordinary public URLs reach it. No browser is actually opened.
sourceAudit.errorBoundary: Only application ServiceError instances retain guidance at IPC; arbitrary thrown objects do not qualify by having a code field.

pairedDecision.Boris: Supports execute normalization plus independent workflow/history/logger defenses and a durable legacy cleanup. Objected to relying solely on a future ordinary state write for migration durability.
pairedDecision.Nadia: Initially preferred execute-only normalization; after challenge accepted the distinct workflow/settlement failure and log boundaries. Supports preserving provably known no-news/partial-coverage legacy guidance.
pairedDecision.Morgan: Use both persistence boundaries, fixed logs, typed IPC errors and a durable versioned migration. Preserve typed legacy no-story/partial-coverage reasons; genericize ambiguous old failure text.
pairedDecision.actualReview: Nadia identified migration-write ENOENT being treated as a missing index; corrected and covered by fault/retry checks. Final review found no actionable issue, including media import graph and the MIME guard.
pairedDecision.reservation: The non-audio rejection, like existing provider status-error branches, does not explicitly drain a rejected body. This was a non-blocking resource note, not a safety/correctness finding.

fixtureCorrections: Corrected temporary media URL assertion syntax.
Made the repeated owned migration-directory setup idempotent.
Only the explicit fault phase claims failed-write retry in its report.
limits: All secret values, upstream failures and provider responses are synthetic. No personal credential, real provider request or actual credential exposure was observed.
This is scoped source/runtime boundary verification, not exhaustive penetration testing or proof against a compromised OS or provider deliberately publishing secrets as valid content.
The non-audio guard accepts audio types, generic binary and missing headers; it is not full audio-codec validation. Existing playback recovery retains that scope.
No deferred size/zoom checks, observed listener session or overall completion/percentage claim.

Migration fault/retry is exercised at the store APIs in actual native Electron processes. The existing main startup initializer can quit on news initialization failure; a friendly startup recovery flow is not established by these checks and remains under broader Q08/Q10 review.
